entries.title: Armenian at a glance
body: Armenian forms its own branch of the Indo-European family. It has two standard forms: Eastern Armenian, spoken in Armenia and Iran, which these cards follow, and Western Armenian, spoken mostly in the diaspora.
There is no grammatical gender. “The” is an ending (-ը or -ն), nouns take case endings instead of prepositions, and most verb tenses are a participle plus a helper verb: գրում եմ, “I write”.

entries.title: The alphabet
body: The Armenian alphabet was created by Mesrop Mashtots around 405 AD with 36 letters; two more, Օ and Ֆ, were added later. Each letter has a capital and a small form.
The sound ու (u) is written with two letters, and և (yev, “and”) is a ligature of ե and ւ.

entries.title: Three kinds of consonant
entries.body: Like Georgian, Armenian has three versions of many stops. Plain ones (կ, պ, տ) have no puff of air and can sound almost like g, b, d to English ears. Aspirated ones (ք, փ, թ, marked with an apostrophe here) have a strong puff. Voiced ones are like English b, d, g.

entries.title: Punctuation
entries.body: Armenian marks are placed inside the word. The question mark ՞ and the exclamation mark ՜ sit over the stressed vowel of the word being asked or exclaimed. The full stop is ։ (verjaket), the comma is the same as in English, and ՝ (called but) marks a short pause.

entries.title: The helper verb “to be”
entries.body: These forms mean “am, is, are” on their own, and they also build the present and other tenses. The negative adds չ-; for “is not” the form is չի.

entries.title: The present tense
entries.body: Replace the infinitive's -ել or -ալ with -ում and add the helper. In a negative sentence the negative helper comes first: չեմ գրում, “I don't write”.

entries.title: Main cases
entries.body: Nouns take endings for their role. These are the forms of քաղաք (city).

entries.title: Numbers
entries.body: Eleven to nineteen are ten plus the unit: տասնմեկ (11), տասներկու (12). A noun after a number usually stays singular.

entries.title: Ararat and the apricot
entries.body: Mount Ararat, visible from Yerevan across the Turkish border, is the national symbol of Armenia and appears on its coat of arms. The apricot (ծիրան) is thought of as the national fruit, and its colour is in the flag: red, blue and apricot-orange.
